prompt: Write the body (about 120 words) of a letter of representation from a personal injury lawyer to an auto insurer. The client was hurt in a parking lot collision. Ask that all contact go through the law firm, ask for the policy limits, and ask the insurer to keep all evidence. No salutation, no signature, no names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1298; do not mention it.)
text:
This firm represents the injured party in connection with the parking lot collision described in the claim you have opened under the policy issued by your company. Please direct all further communication regarding this matter to our office and do not contact our client directly, whether by telephone, mail, email, or in person. If your insured or any representative of your company has already been in contact with our client, please let us know immediately.

We request that you disclose the bodily injury and property damage liability limits of the policy in force at the time of the incident, together with a certified copy of the declarations page and any excess or umbrella coverage that may apply. Please also confirm the name of the adjuster assigned to this claim.

We further demand that your company preserve all evidence relating to the collision. This includes photographs, video footage, recorded statements, incident reports, telematics or vehicle data, repair estimates, claim notes, and all communications with your insured or any third party. Any destruction or alteration of such material may result in sanctions. Please confirm in writing within ten days that this preservation obligation has been acknowledged and implemented.
